text:
carlos.cs: customer reported sudden p99 spike for embeddings in us-west-2 ~03:40 UTC. baseline p99 ~150ms, now ~1.2s. they see timeouts and higher error rates. escalating.

sarah.oncall: on it. which model/route? any tenant id or request ids?

carlos.cs: route: /v1/embeddings/redwood-open-embed-512, tenant acme-marketing, sample req id 0001f3a2. repro attached by customer (small loop) — they say it started after maintenance window.

miguel.sre: looking at infra metrics. host CPU iowait and NFS retransmits spike coincident with p99. also GPU device driver logs show repeated microcode reloads on some nodes.

miguel.sre: quick graph links: https://grafana.redwood/graph?panel=p99-embeds-usw2

anya.ml: customer-reported payloads are small (single input ~512 tokens). shouldn't drive IO. suspect KV cache misses + filesystem backing of checkpoint shards -> NFS reads + GPU stall.

carlos.cs: customer says they didn't change anything. maintenance window included kernel preempt patch + microcode/firmware refresh on pool nodes.

jen.support: assigning priority P1 for customer SLA impact. any immediate mitigation?

miguel.sre: trying to reproduce on a spare node in same pool with firmware 2.1.4 + kernel v5.19-preempt. quick repro script:

```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"test text"}' &
done
wait
```

miguel.sre: repro succeeds: p95 ~200ms, p99 flares to 900-1500ms after ~30s of hammering. dmesg on affected node shows repeated lines:

```
[ 1234.567890] gpu0: microcode reload complete
[ 1234.568002] gpu0: stalled while waiting for host-page pin
[ 1234.568015] nvme0n1: I/O blocked for 1200ms
```

sarah.oncall: mhmm. pattern suggests microcode+host kernel preempt interplay causing short stalls and kicking up p99. NFS retransmits explain storage side.

anya.ml: immediate customer-facing mitigation: route this customer's traffic to us-west-1 cluster (no firmware/kernel combo there) or switch them to a CPU-embedding fallback (higher latency baseline but stable) while we patch.

carlos.cs: customer prefers us-west-1 fallback. can we cutover at infra level quickly?

miguel.sre: yes — we can add a route override for tenant acme-marketing -> us-west-1. doing a canary: moving 10% now.

infra-bot: deploy started: route-override-service v2 -> acme-marketing 10% -> us-west-1 (job 8923)

miguel.sre: canary looks good for that 10% (p99 back to ~140ms). ramping to 100% over 5m.

infra-bot: deploy update: 50%

sarah.oncall: while canary ramps, escalation plan: 1) roll back microcode on affected pool to previous stable build (2.1.2) 2) set node kernel param vm.swappiness and nfs mount options to reduce retransmits 3) taint affected nodes to prevent new allocations until investigated.

miguel.sre: executing taint and rollback prep. rollback commands (internal):

```
ssh node-47
sudo nvfwctl rollback --slot=previous
systemctl restart redwood-runtime
kubectl taint nodes node-47 redwood/unstable=true:NoSchedule
```

carlos.cs: customer update posted: thanks for quick action — they see improvement for traffic routed to us-west-1, but still worrying.

miguel.sre: completed taint on 4 nodes in pool. initiated microcode rollback on 2 nodes (in progress). monitoring.

anya.ml: small note for postmortem: investigate KV cache eviction policy under short stalls — could amplify NFS read bursts.

miguel.sre: after rollback on node-47 p99 back to ~160ms. affected nodes show reduced dmesg stalls.

sarah.oncall: mitigation worked. keep routing override for 30m to ensure stability, then we can slowly unroute and observe.

jen.support: customer notified and ticket updated. kudos team. follow-ups: patch release with microcode + kernel compatibility tests, add NFS retransmit alerting, run KV cache stress test, and update runbook for similar cross-surface maintenance.

carlos.cs: marking customer ticket as mitigated, they'll keep monitoring. will reopen if issues persist.

miguel.sre: next steps: full rollback of firmware to stable on remaining nodes overnight, reproduce with controlled load tests, and bake preflight check before firmware push. assigned to miguel.sre.

anya.ml: I'll own the postmortem and add prompts/benchmarks for embedding workloads.

sarah.oncall: thanks all. closing incident thread once postmortem doc created. :white_check_mark:
